family_title: Initialization (base-point splitting) and rank allocation for low-rank adapters

methods.name: PiSSA
methods.full_name: Principal Singular values and Singular vectors Adaptation
methods.paper_title: PiSSA: Principal Singular Values and Singular Vectors Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_0=U S V^\top,\quad B=U_{[:,:r]}S_{[:r,:r]}^{1/2},\quad A=S_{[:r,:r]}^{1/2}V_{[:,:r]}^\top,\quad W^{res}=U_{[:,r:]}S_{[r:,r:]}V_{[:,r:]}^\top=W_0-BA,\qquad h=(W^{res}+BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (attention and MLP projections)
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space (\Delta W = BA - B_0A_0); the base point is moved from W_0 to the rank-(\min(d_{in},d_{out})-r) residual W^{res} and the adapter starts on the principal rank-r SVD component of W_0
methods.mergeable_reason: W^{res}+BA is a dense matrix of the original shape; to ship as a plain LoRA on the untouched W_0 the paper converts it to \Delta W=[B'\ B][A';-A] at rank 2r.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W^{res}+B_0A_0=W_0 by construction (data-free truncated SVD of W_0; fast randomized SVD makes it seconds).
methods.key_idea: Instead of zero-initializing the adapter, put the top-r singular triplets of W_0 into the trainable factors and freeze the residual, so training updates the directions that matter most and converges faster; the residual also quantizes better (QPiSSA).
methods.results_note: Reported consistent gains over LoRA on 11 models (184M-70B), e.g. GSM8K 53.22 vs 42.85 on LLaMA-2-7B and 77.78 vs 74.53 on Gemma-7B; QPiSSA on LLaMA-3-70B reaches 86.05 vs 81.73 for QLoRA.

relations.note: same BA parameterization, only the initialization and base point change
PiSSA trains the top-r singular components, MiLoRA the bottom-r
CorDA instruction-previewed mode with covariance C=I reduces to PiSSA
OLoRA uses a QR instead of an SVD factorization of W_0
QPiSSA and LoftQ both reduce quantization error by splitting W_0 into a quantized residual plus a low-rank adapter

methods.name: MiLoRA
methods.paper_title: MiLoRA: Harnessing Minor Singular Components for Parameter-Efficient LLM Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: W_0=\sum_{i}\sigma_i u_i v_i^\top=W_p+W_m,\quad W_m=\sum_{i>k-r}\sigma_i u_i v_i^\top=\underbrace{U_m\Sigma_m^{1/2}}_{B}\,\underbrace{\Sigma_m^{1/2}V_m^\top}_{A},\qquad h=(W_p+BA)\,x;\ W_p\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer (attention and MLP projections)
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space; base point W_p is the rank-(k-r) principal truncation of W_0 (k=\min(d_{in},d_{out})) and the adapter is initialized on the r smallest singular triplets
methods.mergeable_reason: W_p+BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W_p+B_0A_0=W_0 by construction (data-free SVD of W_0); no extra scaling hyperparameter is needed.
methods.key_idea: Keep the principal subspace (assumed to store pretrained knowledge) frozen and adapt only within the minor singular subspace, which is less likely to interfere with pretrained abilities.
methods.results_note: Reported gains over LoRA on LLaMA-2-7B / LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning (+1.6 / +1.1), math reasoning (+2.0), instruction following and LLaVA-1.5 visual instruction tuning.

relations.note: bottom-r instead of top-r singular components
CorDA knowledge-preserved mode with C=I reduces to MiLoRA
KaSA also acts on the minor singular subspace, but discards it and relearns it with a learnable singular-value diagonal
MiCA also targets minor components but freezes B=U_{-r} and trains only A from zero

methods.name: OLoRA
methods.paper_title: OLoRA: Orthonormal Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_0=QR,\quad B=Q_{[:,1:r]},\quad A=R_{[1:r,:]},\quad W^{res}=W_0-\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA,\qquad h=(W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space; B starts with orthonormal columns (first r columns of the QR factor Q of W_0) and A with the first r rows of the upper-triangular factor R
methods.mergeable_reason: W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: the frozen base is translated to W_0-\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_0A_0 so the sum equals W_0 (data-free QR of W_0).
methods.key_idea: Use a cheap QR decomposition of W_0 to give the adapter an orthonormal starting basis, which the author argues improves conditioning, stability and convergence speed.
methods.results_note: Reported higher final accuracy than LoRA in 53 of 60 model/task/rank settings on six commonsense benchmarks for Mistral-7B, LLaMA-2-7B, TinyLlama-1.1B, Gemma-2B and OPT-1.3B.

relations.note: QR-based instead of SVD-based base-point splitting of W_0
same BA adapter, different initialization

methods.name: LoRA-GA
methods.paper_title: LoRA-GA: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
methods.formula_latex: G=\nabla_{W}\mathcal{L}(W_0)=USV^\top,\quad A_0=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\sqrt{\gamma}}V_{[:,1:r]}^\top,\quad B_0=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\sqrt{\gamma}}U_{[:,r+1:2r]},\quad W^{res}=W_0-\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}B_0A_0,\qquad h=(W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space; A and B are initialized from disjoint blocks of the top-2r singular vectors of a sampled full gradient so that the first LoRA step \eta^2(G A_0^\top A_0+B_0B_0^\top G) best approximates \zeta G
methods.mergeable_reason: W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape (but the base differs from W_0, so the adapter alone is not a LoRA on W_0).
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: the offset W_0-\eta B_0A_0 cancels the nonzero adapter; initialization is gradient-driven (one sampled batch, layer-by-layer backward for O(1) memory) with the stable scale factor \sqrt[4]{d_{out}}/\sqrt{\gamma} (paired with \eta=\alpha/\sqrt r) chosen so that forward and backward magnitudes stay rank- and width-stable.
methods.key_idea: Choose A and B from the SVD of the full-fine-tuning gradient so that the very first LoRA update is the best low-rank approximation of the full-fine-tuning update, with a rank- and width-stable scale.
methods.results_note: Reported +5.69% over LoRA on a GLUE subset with T5-Base and +0.34 / +11.52 / +5.05 points on MT-Bench / GSM8K / HumanEval with LLaMA-2-7B, converging 2-4x faster than LoRA.

relations.note: same adapter, gradient-aligned initialization
LoRA-One argues LoRA-GA's use of singular vectors r+1..2r for B leaves the iterates outside the target subspace
gradient-driven vs weight-driven SVD splitting of W_0
GoRA reuses the gradient-driven idea but without offsetting W_0

methods.name: EVA
methods.paper_title: Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning via Explained Variance Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: X^{\ell}\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times d_{in}}\ \text{(activations)}=U\Sigma V^\top\ \text{(incremental SVD)},\quad A^{\ell}=V_{[:,:r_\ell]}^\top,\quad B^{\ell}=0,\quad \xi_j=\frac{\sigma_j^2}{(M-1)\lVert\sigma\rVert_1},\quad \{r_\ell\}=\text{top-}Nr\text{ of }\{\xi_j^\ell\}_{j\le \rho r},\qquad h=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r_\ell}B^{\ell}A^{\ell}x;\ W_0\text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r_\ell(d_{in}+d_{out}),\ \ \textstyle\sum_\ell r_\ell\le N r,\ r_\ell\le\rho r
methods.locus: any linear layer; ranks redistributed across all adapted layers
methods.structure: \Delta W=BA with A spanning the top right-singular (principal input-activation) directions of the downstream data; per-layer rank r_\ell chosen by globally ranking explained-variance ratios
methods.mergeable_reason: Plain LoRA update on an untouched W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B=0 (W_0 untouched); A is data-driven: top right-singular vectors of minibatch input activations, computed by incremental SVD until cosine similarity of successive estimates exceeds a threshold \tau.
methods.key_idea: Initialize the down-projection on the directions of maximal input-activation variance for the downstream task and redistribute a fixed rank budget to the layers whose activations have the most explainable variance.
methods.results_note: Reported the highest average score among LoRA initializations across 51 tasks spanning language generation/understanding, image classification and RL, with initialization costing about 0.7% of training time.

relations.note: B=0 initialization kept; only A and ranks change
both use input-activation statistics, but EVA keeps W_0 untouched
rank allocation done once before training instead of by pruning during training
EVA uses principal input-activation directions, Astra tail output-activation directions

methods.name: CorDA
methods.paper_title: CorDA: Context-Oriented Decomposition Adaptation of Large Language Models for Task-Aware Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: C=XX^\top\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{in}},\quad \mathrm{SVD}(W_0C)=U\Sigma V^\top,\quad W_0=U\Sigma(V^\top C^{-1});\ \ \text{IPM: }B=U_{[:,:r]}\Sigma_{[:r]}^{1/2},\ A=\Sigma_{[:r]}^{1/2}(V^\top C^{-1})_{[:r,:]};\ \ \text{KPM: same with the last }r\text{ components};\quad W'=W_0-BA,\ \ h=(W'+BA)x;\ W'\text{ frozen}
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space; the base point is split along the singular directions of W_0C (covariance-whitened weight), i.e. a generalized SVD of W_0 w.r.t. the input-activation metric C
methods.mergeable_reason: W'+BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W'+B_0A_0=W_0 because the C^{-1} factor undoes the covariance orientation; data-driven (covariance from a few hundred task or QA samples).
methods.key_idea: Orient the weight decomposition by the covariance of activations from either the downstream task (instruction-previewed mode: train the dominant components) or world-knowledge data (knowledge-preserved mode: train the least-used components to limit forgetting).
methods.results_note: Reported IPM GSM8K 53.90 / MATH 8.52 vs PiSSA 51.48 / 7.60 on LLaMA-2-7B, KPM preserving more NQ-open knowledge than LoRA, and best GLUE average (83.38) with RoBERTa-base.

relations.note: IPM with C=I is PiSSA
KPM with C=I is MiLoRA
LoRA-Null pushes the knowledge-preserving idea to the null space of activations
both data-driven initializations from activation statistics

methods.name: KaSA
methods.paper_title: KaSA: Knowledge-Aware Singular-Value Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_0=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_iu_iv_i^\top,\quad W_{world}=\sum_{i=1}^{k-r}\sigma_iu_iv_i^\top,\qquad W=W_{world}+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B\,\mathrm{diag}(\Delta\sigma)\,A,\qquad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\textstyle\sum_j\Delta\sigma_j^2+\gamma\big(\lVert B^\top B-I_r\rVert_F+\lVert AA^\top-I_r\rVert_F\big);\ W_{world}\text{ frozen},\ B,\Delta\sigma,A\text{ trained}
methods.structure: SVD-shaped update \Delta W=B\,\mathrm{diag}(\Delta\sigma)\,A with soft orthogonality on B,A and a learnable singular-value vector, added on top of a base whose r smallest singular components were removed
methods.mergeable_reason: B diag(Δσ) A is a dense d_out×d_in matrix that folds into the (truncated) base, though the truncation itself is irreversible.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exact: B=0 makes the adapter zero, but the base is permanently truncated by the r smallest singular components (a small, data-free perturbation of W_0).
methods.key_idea: Treat the smallest singular components of W_0 as task-irrelevant noise, discard them, and relearn that subspace with an explicitly SVD-shaped adapter whose singular values are learned and regularized.
methods.results_note: Reported outperforming 14 PEFT baselines on GLUE (86.3 average with RoBERTa-base at about 0.24% trainable parameters), instruction following and commonsense benchmarks.

relations.note: same P\Lambda Q-style SVD parameterization with orthogonality regularizer
both operate on the minor singular subspace of W_0
SVD-based base-point modification

methods.name: LoRA-One
methods.paper_title: LoRA-One: One-Step Full Gradient Could Suffice for Fine-Tuning Large Language Models, Provably and Efficiently
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space and is initialized to the best rank-r approximation of one full-batch negative gradient (a truncated gradient step); optional Riemannian/ScaledGD preconditioners (B^\top B)^{-1},(AA^\top)^{-1}
methods.mergeable_reason: Plain additive low-rank update on W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No: W_0 is not offset, so the initial model equals one best rank-r full-batch gradient-descent step from W_0 (gradient-driven spectral initialization from a large sampled batch).
methods.key_idea: Theory shows LoRA iterates align with the top singular subspace of the one-step full fine-tuning gradient, so initializing there (and preconditioning against ill-conditioning) achieves the alignment immediately; it also corrects LoRA-GA's choice of singular vectors.
methods.results_note: Reported 88.73 vs 82.72 GLUE average over LoRA (T5-base) and 28.66 vs 25.85 HumanEval, with negligible time/memory overhead.

relations.note: gradient-SVD initialization, but uses the top-r subspace for both factors and no weight offset
both initialize the adapter as a low-rank approximation of the first full-FT update
GoRA also starts at an approximate gradient step without offsetting W_0

methods.name: GoRA
methods.paper_title: GoRA: Gradient-driven Adaptive Low Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: \bar G=\tfrac1N\textstyle\sum_i\partial\mathcal{L}_i/\partial W_0,\quad I(W)=\mathrm{avg}(|W_0\odot\bar G|),\quad r_\ell=\big\lfloor b\,a_\ell/\sqrt{d_{in}+d_{out}}\big\rfloor\in[r_{min},r_{max}],\ a_\ell=\tfrac{I(W_\ell)}{\sum_j I(W_j)};\quad A_0\sim\text{Kaiming},\ B_0=-\xi\,\bar G A_0^\top(A_0A_0^\top)^{-1},\qquad W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r_\ell}BA
methods.locus: any linear layer; ranks allocated across all adapted layers
methods.structure: \Delta W=BA with per-layer rank r_\ell set by gradient sensitivity; B_0 is the least-squares solution making B_0A_0 the best approximation of -\bar G in the row space of the random A_0
methods.mergeable_reason: Plain additive low-rank update on W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No: W_0 is not offset; the initial adapter approximates a (scaled, \xi=\gamma\sqrt{m}/\alpha in the paper's notation) gradient-descent step computed from accumulated gradients on a small data subset.
methods.key_idea: A single accumulated-gradient pass before training is used twice: to allocate ranks across layers by gradient sensitivity and to initialize B so that the adapter starts as a compressed gradient step, without touching W_0.
methods.results_note: Reported Llama-3.1-8B-Base GSM8K 75.74 vs full fine-tuning 73.69 and HumanEval 52.03 vs 51.63 at reference rank 128.

relations.note: uses AdaLoRA-style |w \cdot \nabla w| sensitivity, but computed once before training
gradient-driven initialization, without the training-inference weight offset
both pre-allocate ranks before training from a calibration pass

methods.name: LoRA-SB
methods.paper_title: Initialization using Update Approximation is a Silver Bullet for Extremely Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_{avg}=-\eta\,\mathrm{sign}\Big(\textstyle\sum_i\nabla_W\mathcal{L}(W_0,x_i)\Big)=USV^\top,\quad B=U_{[:,1:r]},\ A=V_{[:,1:r]}^\top,\ R_0=\tfrac1s S_{[1:r,1:r]},\qquad W=W_0+s\,BRA;\ B,A\text{ frozen},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\text{ trained}
methods.structure: \Delta W=BRA with frozen orthonormal outer factors B,A (from the SVD of an approximate first full-FT update) and a trainable r\times r core R
methods.mergeable_reason: BRA is a dense matrix of the original shape and folds into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No: W_0 is not offset, so the model starts at W_0 plus the optimal rank-r approximation of the simulated first AdamW step (sign of summed gradients over ~0.1% of the training data).
methods.key_idea: With the LoRA-XS architecture (frozen B,A, trainable r×r R), initializing B,A from the SVD of an approximate full-FT update makes the learning dynamics hyperparameter-free in the scale s and gives the optimal low-rank approximation of full-FT gradients.
methods.results_note: Reported beating LoRA with 27-90x fewer trainable parameters and comprehensively outperforming LoRA-XS on GSM8K/MATH, commonsense reasoning and GLUE with RoBERTa-large, Llama-3.2-3B, Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-9B.

relations.note: same W_0+sBRA architecture; replaces LoRA-XS's SVD-of-W_0 bases with SVD-of-update bases
both initialize at a rank-r approximation of the first full-FT update
gradient-based initialization

methods.name: LoftQ
methods.paper_title: LoftQ: LoRA-Fine-Tuning-Aware Quantization for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\lVert W_0-Q-BA\rVert_F:\quad Q_t=q_N(W_0-B_{t-1}A_{t-1}),\ \ W_0-Q_t=\textstyle\sum_i\sigma_{t,i}u_{t,i}v_{t,i}^\top,\ \ B_t=[\sqrt{\sigma_{t,i}}u_{t,i}]_{i\le r},\ A_t=[\sqrt{\sigma_{t,i}}v_{t,i}^\top]_{i\le r};\qquad h=(Q_T+BA)x;\ Q_T\text{ frozen (N-bit)},\ A,B\text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of a quantized model
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space; the base point is an N-bit quantized matrix Q and the adapter is initialized to the rank-r SVD of the quantization residual, alternating T times
methods.mergeable_reason: BA can be added to the dequantized Q, but the merged matrix is no longer N-bit unless re-quantized, which reintroduces error.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q_T+B_TA_T\approx W_0 (much closer than QLoRA's Q+0); data-free alternating quantization/SVD.
methods.key_idea: When the base will be quantized, choose the quantized base and the low-rank adapter jointly so that their sum best approximates W_0, instead of zero-initializing the adapter on top of an inaccurate quantized weight.
methods.results_note: Reported large gains over QLoRA at low bit widths, e.g. about 8% on MNLI and over 10% on SQuAD v1.1 at 2-bit, and convergence where QLoRA fails.

relations.note: same quantized-base + LoRA setting with a better joint initialization
QPiSSA also lowers quantization error by quantizing the SVD residual

methods.name: Astra
methods.paper_title: Astra: Activation-Space Tail-Eigenvector Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{Cov}(y)=\mathbb{E}[yy^\top]-\mathbb{E}[y]\mathbb{E}[y]^\top=Q\Lambda Q^\top,\ y=W_0x,\quad B_0=Q_{tail}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_0=Q_{tail}^\top W_0,\quad W^{res}=W_0-B_0A_0=(I-Q_{tail}Q_{tail}^\top)W_0,\qquad h=(W^{res}+BA)x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen}
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space whose output side starts on the r tail eigenvectors (smallest eigenvalues) of the output-activation covariance; the base is W_0 projected off that subspace
methods.mergeable_reason: W^{res}+BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: B_0A_0=Q_{tail}Q_{tail}^\top W_0 is subtracted from the base; data-driven from a small calibration set (e.g. 64 samples).
methods.key_idea: Characterize each layer by the output activations it produces on the downstream task and place the trainable update in the under-used tail eigenspace of those activations, which preserves dominant behaviour while giving room for task adaptation.
methods.results_note: Reported outperforming LoRA/PiSSA/CorDA-style baselines on 16 NLU and NLG benchmarks at equal or lower rank, sometimes surpassing full fine-tuning.

relations.note: both are data-driven, output-preserving base-point splits; Astra uses output- instead of input-activation statistics
tail output-activation directions vs principal input-activation directions
both adapt in a minor/tail subspace

methods.name: LoRA-Null
methods.full_name: LoRA initialized in the Null space of activations
methods.paper_title: Put the Space of LoRA Initialization to the Extreme to Preserve Pre-trained Knowledge
methods.formula_latex: X_{pre}=U\Sigma V^\top,\ U_{null}=U_{[:,-r:]}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r},\quad W_0U_{null}U_{null}^\top=U'\Sigma'V'^\top,\quad B=U'_{[:,:r]}\Sigma'^{1/2}_{[:r]},\ A=\Sigma'^{1/2}_{[:r]}V'^\top_{[:r,:]},\quad W_0'=W_0-BA,\qquad h=(W_0'+BA)x
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space initialized as the projection of W_0 onto the (approximate) null space of pre-training-knowledge input activations
methods.mergeable_reason: W_0'+BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W_0'+B_0A_0=W_0; data-driven from activations of knowledge-probing (pre-training-like) data.
methods.key_idea: Argues that the space in which LoRA is initialized, not the residual weight, governs forgetting, and initializes the adapter in the null space of pre-trained-knowledge activations so that updates minimally disturb what the model already knows.
methods.results_note: Reported better knowledge preservation than CorDA (e.g. 93.18% vs 89.00% on LLaMA-3.2-3B math setting) with competitive downstream accuracy.

relations.note: extends CorDA's knowledge-preserved mode from small covariance-oriented components to the activation null space
knowledge preservation by adapting in a minor subspace

methods.name: MiCA
methods.paper_title: MiCA Learns More Knowledge Than LoRA and Full Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W_0=U\Sigma V^\top,\quad B=U_{[:,-r:]}\ \text{(frozen)},\quad A_0=0\ \text{(trained)},\qquad W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA
methods.structure: \Delta W=BA with the output side fixed to the r minor left singular vectors of W_0, i.e. the column space of \Delta W is pinned to a frozen minor subspace and only the r\times d_{in} map into it is learned
methods.mergeable_reason: Plain additive low-rank update on an untouched W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: A=0 with W_0 untouched (data-free SVD of W_0 for the frozen B).
methods.key_idea: Freeze the output basis to the least-used singular directions of W_0 and learn only the input map, halving parameters versus LoRA while targeting a more plastic subspace for new knowledge.
methods.results_note: Reported higher knowledge-acquisition accuracy than LoRA on Llama-2-7B and Qwen-2.5-7B (e.g. 61.33 vs 58.28 on a BLOGS set and 39.2 vs 29.4 on a German HISTORY set).

relations.note: minor singular subspace, but frozen B and zero A instead of an offset base
also freezes one factor; here the frozen factor is the minor output basis

methods.name: rsLoRA
methods.paper_title: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\gamma_r BA,\quad \gamma_r=\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}\ \ (\text{instead of }\tfrac{\alpha}{r}),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}
methods.structure: same \Delta W=BA as LoRA; only the scalar multiplier changes so that activations and gradients stay \Theta(1) as r grows
methods.mergeable_reason: Identical to LoRA up to a scalar.
methods.identity_at_init: B=0 as in LoRA.
methods.key_idea: Shows that the standard alpha/r scaling makes higher-rank adapters learn too slowly (gradient collapse), and that alpha/sqrt(r) is the rank-stable choice that lets larger ranks actually help.

relations.note: changes only the rank-dependent scaling factor
LoRA-GA adopts \eta=\alpha/\sqrt r and derives its own stable scale

methods.name: AdaLoRA
methods.paper_title: AdaLoRA: Adaptive Budget Allocation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.hf_peft_config: AdaLoraConfig(init_r, target_r, tinit, tfinal, deltaT, beta1, beta2, orth_reg_weight, total_step)
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+P\Lambda Q,\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda_i),\ Q\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\quad R(P,Q)=\lVert P^\top P-I\rVert_F^2+\lVert QQ^\top-I\rVert_F^2;\quad S_{k,i}=s(\lambda_{k,i})+\tfrac1{d_{out}}\textstyle\sum_js(P_{k,ji})+\tfrac1{d_{in}}\sum_js(Q_{k,ij}),\ s=\bar I\cdot\bar U,\ I(w)=|w\,\nabla_w\mathcal{L}|;\quad \lambda_{k,i}\leftarrow0\ \text{unless }S_{k,i}\in\text{top-}b^{(t)}
methods.locus: any linear layer; budget shared across all adapted matrices
methods.structure: SVD-shaped update \Delta W=P\Lambda Q with soft-orthogonal P,Q and a diagonal of singular values that is masked (pruned) by a global importance ranking under a cubic budget schedule
methods.mergeable_reason: P\Lambda Q is a dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: \Lambda=0 (P,Q random Gaussian); importance scores are EMA-smoothed sensitivity times uncertainty.
methods.key_idea: Parameterize each update in SVD form so that rank can be reduced by zeroing singular values without expensive SVDs, and move rank budget to the matrices whose triplets are most important for the loss.
methods.results_note: Reported better or on-par GLUE results vs LoRA at all budgets with DeBERTaV3-base and a 1.2% F1 gain on SQuAD 2.0 with under 0.1% trainable parameters.

relations.note: fixed uniform-rank LoRA is AdaLoRA with no pruning
IncreLoRA grows ranks with the same style of importance score instead of pruning them
SoRA prunes ranks with a proximal L1 gate instead of sensitivity scores
ElaLoRA adds rank expansion to AdaLoRA's pruning

methods.name: DyLoRA
methods.paper_title: DyLoRA: Parameter Efficient Tuning of Pre-trained Models using Dynamic Search-Free Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: b\sim p_B\ \text{on}\ \{r_{min},\dots,r_{max}\},\quad h=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha}{b}\,B_{[:,1:b]}A_{[1:b,:]}\,x,\quad \mathcal{L}^{DY}_{\downarrow b}=\textstyle\sum_i\ell\big(f(x_i;A_{[1:b,:]},B_{[:,1:b]}),y_i\big)
methods.structure: nested family of truncations \Delta W_{\downarrow b}=B_{[:,1:b]}A_{[1:b,:]} trained jointly (nested-dropout-like ordering of rank-1 components), so every prefix rank is a usable adapter
methods.mergeable_reason: After choosing any rank b at deployment, B_{[:,1:b]}A_{[1:b,:]} folds into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (up-projection B=0).
methods.key_idea: Train a single adapter for a whole range of ranks by sampling a truncation rank at every step, so the rank can be chosen after training without a search.
methods.results_note: Reported training 4-7x faster than searching LoRA ranks, with GLUE average 86.66 vs 86.49 for LoRA on RoBERTa-base.

relations.note: a DyLoRA adapter truncated at rank b is a rank-b LoRA
search-free rank flexibility vs importance-based budget allocation

methods.name: SoRA
methods.paper_title: Sparse Low-rank Adaptation of Pre-trained Language Models
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0x+B\big(g\odot(Ax)\big),\ g\in\mathbb{R}^{r_{max}};\quad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_0+\lambda\textstyle\sum_k\lVert g^{(k)}\rVert_1;\quad g_{t+1}=\mathcal{T}_{\eta_t\lambda}\big(g_t-\eta_t\nabla_g\mathcal{L}_0\big),\ \mathcal{T}_\xi(x)=\mathrm{sign}(x)\max(|x|-\xi,0)
methods.trainable_params: r_{max}(d_{in}+d_{out}+1)\ \text{during training};\ r'(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{after pruning zero gates}
methods.structure: \Delta W=B\,\mathrm{diag}(g)\,A with a sparse gate vector driven to exact zeros by proximal (soft-thresholding) updates; zeroed rank-1 components are removed
methods.mergeable_reason: After pruning, B diag(g) A is a plain low-rank matrix that folds into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B=0 as in LoRA (A Kaiming-uniform, gate g ~ N(0,1) in the official code).
methods.key_idea: Start with a generous rank and let an L1-regularized gate, optimized by proximal gradient, decide how many rank-1 components each matrix keeps.
methods.results_note: Reported GLUE average 89.36 with 0.91M parameters vs LoRA 88.38 (1.33M) and AdaLoRA 88.83 (1.27M) on DeBERTaV3-base, with about 30% faster training.

relations.note: gate sparsity instead of sensitivity-based singular value masking
both gate individual rank-1 components

methods.name: IncreLoRA
methods.paper_title: IncreLoRA: Incremental Parameter Allocation Method for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{r_k}\lambda_i\,b_ia_i^\top,\ \lVert b_ia_i^\top\rVert_F=1;\quad S_k^{(t)}=\mathrm{avg}\big(|\Delta W_k\odot\nabla_{\Delta W_k}\mathcal{L}|\big)\ \text{(EMA-smoothed}\times\text{uncertainty)};\ \text{every }\nu\text{ steps add a rank-1 component to the top-}h\text{ modules};\ R=\lVert A^\top A-I\rVert_F^2+\lVert B^\top B-I\rVert_F^2
methods.locus: any linear layer; budget shared across modules
methods.structure: sum of scaled rank-1 components whose number per module grows during training according to an importance score; each new component is pre-trained as a reserve with tiny scale (advance learning) and gets its own restarted warmup
methods.mergeable_reason: The final sum of rank-1 terms is a dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: \lambda_i=0 for active components (reserve components held at \lambda\approx10^{-5}).
methods.key_idea: Grow, rather than prune, the rank of each module: start every matrix at rank 1 and add components where the importance score says capacity is needed, which avoids AdaLoRA's upper bound on per-module rank.
methods.results_note: Reported GLUE average 89.61 vs AdaLoRA 89.46 at 1.33M parameters on DeBERTaV3-base, with larger advantages at low budgets.

relations.note: incremental growth vs pruning, with AdaLoRA-style sensitivity scores
ElaLoRA both grows and prunes

methods.name: ALoRA
methods.paper_title: ALoRA: Allocating Low-Rank Adaptation for Fine-tuning Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: h=W_0x+B_mG_mA_mx,\ G_m=\mathrm{diag}(\alpha_{m,1},\dots,\alpha_{m,r_m}),\ \alpha'_{m,i}=2\,\sigma(a'_{m,i});\quad \mathrm{IS}(i)=S(\mathcal{M})-S(\mathcal{M}_{\setminus i})+S(\mathcal{M}_{i})
methods.locus: any linear layer; ranks moved between modules
methods.structure: \Delta W=B\,\mathrm{diag}(\alpha)\,A with per-rank gates; rank-1 components with low ablation-based importance are pruned and their budget re-allocated to important modules, iteratively
methods.mergeable_reason: After allocation, each B diag(α) A is a plain low-rank matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B=0); gates relaxed to 2\sigma(a') so a'=0 gives gate 1.
methods.key_idea: Estimate each rank-1 component's importance by ablation (performance with it removed and with it alone) on a validation batch, prune the useless ones, and hand their rank budget to modules that need it.
methods.results_note: Reported outperforming LoRA, SoRA and AdaLoRA at comparable budgets on GLUE/SuperGLUE tasks, E2E and instruction tuning with LLaMA-2-7B.

relations.note: ablation-based instead of sensitivity-based importance
both gate rank-1 components

methods.name: AutoLoRA
methods.full_name: Automatic rank tuning for LoRA via meta-learning
methods.paper_title: AutoLoRA: Automatically Tuning Matrix Ranks in Low-Rank Adaptation Based on Meta Learning
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_\ell=\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^{k_\ell}\alpha_\ell^j\,b_\ell^j a_\ell^{j\top},\quad \alpha_\ell^j=\frac{\exp\beta_\ell^j}{\sum_i\exp\beta_\ell^i};\quad \min_\beta\mathcal{L}_{val}\big(W-\eta\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_{train}(W,\beta)\big);\quad r_\ell=\#\{j:\alpha_\ell^j\ge 1/k_\ell\}
methods.structure: weighted sum of rank-1 components with softmax selection variables learned by bi-level (train / validation) optimization; thresholding selects the rank, then the adapter is retrained
methods.mergeable_reason: The retrained rank-r_\ell update is a plain low-rank matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA-style zero-product initialization of the rank-1 components (not separately specified beyond LoRA).
methods.key_idea: Treat the per-layer rank as a hyperparameter to be meta-learned: selection weights on rank-1 components are fit on validation loss through a one-step-unrolled bi-level problem, then thresholded.
methods.results_note: Reported GLUE average 85.5 vs LoRA 84.9 and AdaLoRA 85.0 with RoBERTa-base at about 0.3M parameters.

relations.note: meta-learned instead of sensitivity-based rank selection
alternative way to avoid manual rank search

methods.name: ElaLoRA
methods.paper_title: ElaLoRA: Elastic & Learnable Low-Rank Adaptation for Efficient Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+P\Lambda Q;\quad S_i=s(\lambda_i)+\tfrac1{d_{out}}\textstyle\sum_js(P_{ji})+\tfrac1{d_{in}}\sum_js(Q_{ij}),\ s(w)=|w\,\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial w|;\ \text{every }t_{adjust}\text{ steps prune the }b^{(t)}\text{ globally least important ranks and expand }b^{(t)}\text{ ranks in matrices whose weakest ranks are most important},\ b^{(t)}=\mathrm{round}\big(b(1-P^3)\big)
methods.structure: AdaLoRA-style SVD-shaped update whose per-matrix rank can both shrink and grow during training; new ranks are Gram-Schmidt orthogonalized
methods.mergeable_reason: P\Lambda Q is a dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: \Lambda=0 as in AdaLoRA; expanded ranks initialized by Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization.
methods.key_idea: Make rank allocation elastic: alongside AdaLoRA-style pruning, re-expand ranks where importance indicates under-capacity, with a cubic schedule that tapers the reallocation.
methods.results_note: Reported GLUE average 88.01 at r=2 exceeding AdaLoRA at r=4 (87.39), plus gains on XSum and VTAB.

relations.note: adds rank expansion to AdaLoRA's pruning
both can grow ranks

methods.name: LoRA-drop
methods.paper_title: LoRA-drop: Efficient LoRA Parameter Pruning based on Output Evaluation
methods.formula_latex: g_i=\textstyle\sum_{x\in D_s}\lVert\Delta W_ix_i\rVert_2^2,\quad I_i=g_i/\sum_jg_j;\quad \text{keep individual }B_iA_i\text{ for the top layers until }\sum I_i\ge T,\ \text{all other layers share one }B_sA_s:\ \ h_i=W_{0,i}x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B_sA_sx
methods.locus: LoRA modules across layers; unimportant layers share one adapter
methods.structure: layer-wise allocation: important layers keep their own rank-r \Delta W_i=B_iA_i, the rest are tied to a single shared rank-r update
methods.mergeable_reason: Each layer's (own or shared) BA folds into its W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B=0); importance measured after a few warm-up steps on about 10% of the data.
methods.key_idea: Judge each layer's LoRA by the actual magnitude of its output on data rather than by parameter statistics, and stop paying for separate adapters in layers whose output contribution is small.
methods.results_note: Reported GLUE average 86.2 vs LoRA 86.1 and full fine-tuning 86.4 on RoBERTa-base while keeping about 50% of the LoRA parameters.

relations.note: layer-level, output-based allocation instead of rank-level sensitivity pruning
same adapters, with cross-layer parameter sharing

methods.name: DoRA (dynamic rank)
methods.full_name: Dynamic Low-Rank Adaptation (Mao et al.; not the weight-decomposed DoRA)
methods.paper_title: DoRA: Enhancing Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Dynamic Rank Distribution
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{r'}c_i\,b_ia_i^\top,\ b_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}},a_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}};\quad s_i=\frac{\lVert c_ib_ia_i^\top\rVert_F}{\lVert\sum_jc_jb_ja_j^\top\rVert_F}\ \text{(EMA-smoothed)};\ \text{prune by }c_i\leftarrow0\ \text{under a cubic budget }b^{(0)}=r'\to b^{(T)}=r;\quad R_{DEM}=\tfrac1n\textstyle\sum_i(\mathrm{Var}(a_i)+\mathrm{Var}(b_i))
methods.locus: any linear layer; budget shared across matrices
methods.structure: sum of scaled rank-1 components pruned by their Frobenius-norm share of the layer update; pruned components can revive
methods.mergeable_reason: The retained sum of rank-1 terms is a dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: c_i=0 (a_i,b_i Kaiming-initialized).
methods.key_idea: Decompose each LoRA layer into single-rank components and prune by how much each actually contributes to the layer's update norm, with a variance regularizer that keeps component entries balanced.
methods.results_note: Reported outperforming LoRA by 0.84-0.88 and AdaLoRA by 0.45-0.59 points on GLUE, plus SQuAD and XSum results with RoBERTa and BART, at under 0.3% trainable parameters.

relations.note: same cubic budget schedule, norm-based component importance using both factors
rank-1 component allocation

methods.name: AdaMSS
methods.paper_title: AdaMSS: Adaptive Multi-Subspace Approach for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \hat W_0=U_{[:,1:R]}S_{[1:R]}V_{[:,1:R]}^\top,\ \text{output units clustered into }K\text{ subspaces }\mathcal{S}_k;\quad \Delta W_{\mathcal{S}_k,:}=C_k\,B_k\,\tilde A_k,\ \tilde A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{R_k\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen orthonormal},\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times R_k}\ \text{(QR-orthogonal init)},\ C_k\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{S}_k|\times r_k},\ C_k=0;\ \text{ASA keeps the top-}K_t\text{ blocks by AdaLoRA-style importance}
methods.structure: block-structured low-rank update: the principal rank-R part of W_0 is segmented (low-rank-representation clustering) into K subspaces, each receiving its own tiny low-rank update A_kB_kC_k; whole subspaces are frozen by adaptive subspace allocation
methods.mergeable_reason: The scattered block updates form a dense matrix of the original shape (HF PEFT implements merge).
methods.identity_at_init: C_k=0 (W_0 untouched); frozen bases come from a data-free truncated SVD of W_0 plus subspace clustering.
methods.key_idea: The principal row space of a pretrained weight decomposes into several smaller subspaces; adapting each with its own small rank and pruning irrelevant subspaces gives a tighter generalization bound and far fewer parameters than a single-subspace adapter like PiSSA.
methods.results_note: Reported +4.7% average accuracy over LoRA on seven ViT-Large tasks with 15.4% of its parameters, and +7% over PiSSA on RoBERTa-Large with about 94% fewer trainable parameters.

relations.note: starts from the principal rank-R SVD part of W_0, then segments it
uses AdaLoRA's sensitivity-uncertainty importance and cubic schedule at the level of subspaces

papers.title: The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics
papers.claim: Of the two zero-product initializations, (A random, B=0) and (A=0, B random), the first permits larger stable learning rates and yields more efficient feature learning, so it performs better on average; the two are not equivalent despite both giving BA=0.
papers.relevance: Shows that the choice of base point within the zero-update fibre {(B,A): BA=0} matters dynamically, which is exactly the degree of freedom the init family exploits; a unified theory must treat initialization as a choice of point in the factor space, not just of \Delta W.

papers.title: On the Crucial Role of Initialization for Matrix Factorization
papers.claim: Nyström initialization (X_0=A\Omega with Gaussian \Omega, Y_0=0) lets ScaledGD converge quadratically for matrix factorization where only linear rates were known; applied to LoRA as NoRA (B_0=W_0\Omega, A_0=0) and NoRA+ (with ScaledGD) it improves fine-tuning of 1B-7B LLMs and diffusion models.
papers.relevance: Provides an optimization-theoretic justification for weight-aware (sketch-of-W_0) initialization and its pairing with preconditioned optimizers, the same pairing LoRA-One uses.

papers.title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
papers.claim: In \Delta W=BA, A acts as an input feature extractor and B maps features to outputs; a random untrained A performs nearly as well as a tuned one, and training only B gives better information-theoretic generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: Explains why initializations that freeze one factor to a fixed basis (LoRA-SB, MiCA, LoRA-XS) lose little, and why the two factors play non-symmetric roles in any categorical description of the adapter.

papers.title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
papers.claim: LoRA-trained weights contain new high-ranking singular vectors ('intruder dimensions') absent from full fine-tuning; LoRA's forgetting is localized in them, and scaling them down restores pre-training behaviour with little loss in task accuracy.
papers.relevance: Gives a spectral diagnostic for how an update interacts with the singular structure of W_0, which is the axis along which PiSSA, MiLoRA, KaSA, CorDA and Astra choose their base points.

papers.title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Fine-tuning has very low intrinsic dimension: optimizing only about 200 parameters randomly projected into the full space recovers 90% of full RoBERTa performance on MRPC, larger and longer-pretrained models have lower intrinsic dimension, and this yields compression-based generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: The empirical foundation for low-rank adaptation and for asking how much rank each layer actually needs, the question rank-allocation methods answer adaptively.

papers.title: A Unified Study of LoRA Variants: Taxonomy, Review, Codebase, and Empirical Evaluation
papers.claim: Organizes LoRA variants along rank, optimization dynamics, initialization and MoE axes, releases a modular codebase (LoRAFactory), and finds that LoRA and its variants are far more sensitive to learning rate than to other hyperparameters and that a well-tuned vanilla LoRA matches or beats most variants.
papers.relevance: A taxonomy whose initialization (weight-, gradient-, activation-driven) and rank-allocation axes coincide with this family, and an important empirical caution that apparent gains of init/rank methods may partly reflect learning-rate tuning.

notes: Scope: 25 methods in two sub-families. (i) Base-point splitting / initialization: PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, LoRA-GA, EVA, CorDA, KaSA, LoRA-One, GoRA, LoRA-SB, LoftQ, Astra, LoRA-Null, MiCA, rsLoRA (rank-dependent scale). (ii) Rank allocation / dynamic rank: AdaLoRA, DyLoRA, SoRA, IncreLoRA, ALoRA, AutoLoRA, ElaLoRA, LoRA-drop, DoRA (dynamic rank, Mao et al.), AdaMSS; EVA and GoRA belong to both. Structural observation for the category-theoretic framing: every init method picks a point (B_0,A_0) in the factor space together with a compensating base W^{res}; three regimes recur: (a) exact splitting W_0=W^{res}+B_0A_0 (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, LoRA-GA, CorDA, Astra, LoRA-Null), (b) zero adapter on untouched W_0 with a chosen A or B (EVA, MiCA, LoRA default), (c) deliberately non-identity starts equal to an approximate first gradient step (LoRA-One, GoRA, LoRA-SB) or approximate identities (LoftQ, KaSA truncation). CorDA with C=I specializes to PiSSA (IPM) and MiLoRA (KPM). Notation translation: PiSSA, LoRA-One, GoRA and AdaMSS papers use row conventions (y=xW, W in R^{d_in x d_out} or W in R^{m x n} with A on the left); formulas were transposed into h=Wx with B in R^{d_out x r}, A in R^{r x d_in}. GoRA's scale xi=gamma*sqrt(m)/alpha is quoted in the paper's own notation. Uncertainties: LoRA-One paper writes sqrt(gamma) factors while the official README writes 1/sqrt(gamma) and Diag(S) without square root; the paper version is used. KaSA's B=0 init is taken from the HF PEFT variant docstring (paper pseudocode is ambiguous). SoRA init (A Kaiming, B=0, gate ~ N(0,1)) taken from the official code. LoRA-SB venue: ICLR 2025 SCOPE workshop; a later ICLR 2026 submission was withdrawn. AdaMSS has no arXiv version (NeurIPS 2025 proceedings + HF PEFT). AutoLoRA/ALoRA/LoRA-drop have no official public repo found. MiCA (2026) is recent with little uptake but is implemented in HF PEFT, hence included at medium confidence. ID choices: 'alora-allocating' avoids collision with HF PEFT's aLoRA (Activated LoRA, 2504.12397, a different method); 'dora-dynamic-rank' avoids collision with weight-decomposed DoRA (2402.09353). Relation targets outside this family: lora, qlora, lora-xs, lora-fa. Cross-family overlaps to deduplicate: LoftQ (quantization family), LoRA-SB (shares LoRA-XS architecture), rsLoRA (could sit with scaling/optimizer methods such as LoRA+), KaSA (also an SVD-structured adapter). HF PEFT (main, 2026) init options verified in source: gaussian, eva, olora, pissa, pissa_niter_k, corda, astra, loftq, orthogonal, mica, lora_ga; plus KasaConfig, AdaLoraConfig, AdamssConfig, use_rslora, rank_pattern/alpha_pattern for manual per-layer ranks. Considered but not included (low uptake or other family): GeLoRA (EMNLP Findings 2025), ARD-LoRA, PRILoRA, QDyLoRA (quantized DyLoRA), SaLoRA, RaLoRA, Bayesian-LoRA, SORSA, NZLoRA, LoRA-DA, TaRA, IGU-LoRA, LoRA-GA^2, HD-PiSSA, GOAT (SVD-init MoE; routing family), SVFT / LoRA-XS / Spectral Adapter (structure families), LoRA-Pro / LoRA+ (optimizer family), NoRA (recorded under papers). Rate limits on arXiv/Semantic Scholar/GitHub APIs were hit; metadata was confirmed via the arXiv API and S2 batch API on retry, and venues via ACL Anthology, NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR pages, AAAI OJS and author repos.
